profiles.name: CRANK
profiles.tagline: TEE BOX ARSON WITH A WEDGE FIRE EXTINGUISHER
profiles.profile: CRANK’s whole deal is that the tee ball keeps trying to file for workers’ comp, and somehow the short game shows up with a crowbar and drags him back into the money. He can absolutely win ugly when the irons and hands get hot, but the floor is still made of banana peels and double bogeys. The profile is volatile in the best and worst way: one week he’s salvaging a mess, the next he’s creating the mess in the first place. That’s not stability. That’s a guy auditioning for chaos and occasionally nailing the callback.

profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.profile: Dan94 is the rare dude who can hit it like a maniac, then make the rest of the card look unreasonable for trying to keep up. The tee ball is a legitimate weapon, and the irons show up enough that the only real question is whether the putter decides to help or just stand there like a useless drinking buddy. He racks up birdies and wins with a kind of shameless violence, but the profile still has some wobble in the short-game and penalty-free self-sabotage department. When he’s on, the field is basically playing for second and a clean shirt.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.tagline: APPROACH GOLF WITH A SIDE OF DAMAGE
profiles.profile: KeithK75 is what happens when a guy keeps finding greens and then acts surprised when the card still looks like a fight. The irons are the loudest part of the file, and the rest of the bag usually behaves well enough to keep him in the hunt. But there’s a recurring little goblin in the mix: some rounds the putter cooperates, some rounds it’s got the personality of a wet paper towel. He can absolutely win the shootout, yet the shape of the profile says he’s happiest when the approach play is doing the heavy lifting and nobody asks too many questions.

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.tagline: PUTTING THE COURSE IN A CHOKEHOLD AND HIS OWN WEDGES IN A HEADLOCK
profiles.profile: BigTime is a messy little science experiment where the tee ball is fine, the approach game is just enough, and the short game/putting combo occasionally shows up dressed as a hostage situation. The numbers scream that the scoring threat is there, but the floor gets torched when the wedges and broomstick lose the plot. He can hang around because the ball striking doesn’t completely collapse, then give it all back with three-putts and extra mess around the greens. It’s not a subtle profile. It’s a guy who keeps inviting bogey to the party and then acts shocked when it steals the silverware.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.tagline: BIRDIE JAGUAR, WITH SOME EXTRA TRUNK DAMAGE
profiles.profile: MattF has the kind of file that says he can absolutely go low when the engine is humming, because the birdie rate is real and the ceiling is not fake. But the week-to-week shape is annoyingly lumpy: one outing he’s clean and competitive, the next he’s leaving approach shots too far away and making the putter work overtime. He’s not a total disaster, just the kind of golfer who can look like a problem for everyone and then immediately remind you that the wheels are still held on with optimism. The upside is there. So is the dented bumper.

profiles.name: HamSammich
profiles.tagline: SHORT GAME CHIROPRACTOR, EVERYTHING ELSE NEEDS A SUSPENSION
profiles.profile: HamSammich lives in the same neighborhood as trouble and usually forgets to leave the neighborhood. The one thing that keeps him from fully eating dirt is a short game that can throw a rope around a bad round and at least make the scoreboard less embarrassing. Everything before that is a bit of a yard sale: not enough clean contact, not enough greens, and way too much double-bogey seasoning. He can pop a good round now and then, but the profile is mostly a reminder that scrambling is a tax, not a business model.
